contexts.story: Open with Chao’s journey as a hook to show how an engineer grew with AI waves, and frame the talk as a practical guide for developers navigating the LLM era.
Describe the traditional AI model-centric world—its linear workflow, clear role boundaries, and pain points—to give the audience a baseline for how different today’s LLM era is.
Show how large models changed the game—from building standalone models to composing systems around powerful base models—and what that means for how teams work.
Explain how problem definition itself has expanded in the LLM era, emphasizing human–AI co-creation and imagining genuinely useful products beyond current model demos.
Move from vision to implementation by showing how to make LLM systems reliable in practice, combining high-ROI prompt tuning with planner–executor architectures to control errors.
Connect system patterns back to people by contrasting engineers and applied scientists, then highlight the high-ROI skills developers should build to thrive in these evolving roles.
Reassure the audience by clarifying where humans still have an edge—system-level thinking and low-level performance—and how embracing change keeps developers relevant as AI advances.
Ground the advice with a concrete example of Chao’s own AI-augmented workflow, showing how to treat specs as a single source of truth and adopt tools in a task-driven way.
Close with a simple, memorable principle—making every step solid—as a compass for how developers should approach their work and learning in the fast-changing AI landscape.
